10. Exceeded · Revenue growth · anchor-year guidance resolved in anchor year
   Guidance [WMT_Q1_2023] For Q2, we expect net sales growth of over 5%, including comp sales growth of 4% to 5% for Walmart U.S. As our confidence builds in our ability to manage cost increases more efficiently, operating income and EPS are expected to be flat to slightly up.
   Target: Q2 FY2023
   Actual [Q2 FY2023] We delivered strong top-line growth with total constant currency revenue up more than 9% in the second quarter.
   Explanation: The actual is above management's stated range (a favorable beat, not an in-range forecast).

   Actual [FY2023] The Walmart U.S. segment had comparable sales growth of 7.5% for the three months ended April 30, 2023, driven by growth in average ticket, including strong food sales and higher inflation impacts in certain merchandise categories, as well as growth in transactions.
   Explanation: A comparable actual is shown, but management specified no tolerance for this approximate target. No pass/fail is inferred.

13. Missed · Revenue growth · anchor-year guidance resolved in anchor year
   Guidance [WMT_Q2_2023] For Q3, we expect net sales growth of about 5%, including comp sales growth of about 3% for Walmart U.S. We're expecting operating income to decline 8% to 10% and adjusted EPS to decline 9% to 11%.
   Target: Q3 FY2023

[WMT_Q2_2022] Walmart U.S. comp sales increased more than 5% in Q2 and more than 14% on a two-year stack basis.
[WMT_Q2_2022] International sales growth was strong, up nearly 13% in constant currency, with strength in India, Mexico and China, while Sam's Club comp sales grew more than 10%, excluding fuel and tobacco.
[WMT_Q2_2022] Gross margin rate declined 22 basis points, reflecting category mix shift at Sam's Club and format mix shifts in international, but Walmart U.S. gross margin increased with favorable mix and strong Walmart Connect results.
[WMT_Q2_2022] Adjusted operating income on a constant currency basis was up 15.1%, leading to strong adjusted EPS of $1.78 with a $0.03 benefit from currency.
[WMT_Q2_2022] Grocery sales were up 6%, including the benefit from modest ticket inflation and increased low double digits on a two-year stack basis.
[WMT_Q2_2022] Walmart U.S. gross profit rate improved 20 basis points with lower markdowns and strong advertising revenue, partially offset by increased supply chain costs.
[10-Q Q4 2022 — Item 5. Other Information] Net sales for the Sam's Club segment increased $2.4 billion or 12.8% and $8.6 billion or 15.9% for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2022, respectively, when compared to the same periods in the previous fiscal year.
[10-Q Q4 2022 — Item 5. Other Information] Gross profit rate decreased 46 and 177 basis points for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2022, respectively, when compared to the same periods in the previous fiscal year.
[10-Q Q4 2022 — Item 5. Other Information] Operating expenses as a percentage of segment net sales decreased 68 and 106 basis points for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2022, respectively, when compared to the same periods in the previous fiscal year, primarily driven by higher sales.
